analyzed_vuln.description: Use-after-free due to duplicated ownership of the same constant array zval in op_array literals. During compilation of the nullsafe property expression in the PoC (`<?['']?->\xff;`), a constant array produced via `zend_try_ct_eval_array()` is inserted into literals such that the same refcounted array ends up referenced by multiple literal slots without proper addref/separation. In `destroy_op_array()` (zend_opcode.c:489), literal destruction runs `zval_ptr_dtor_nogc()` over all literals, causing the array to be freed on first dtor and then decref/read again on a later literal, triggering UAF in `zend_gc_delref()`. Crash site is destroy_op_array, but root cause is incorrect literal/refcount handling in compile-time property compilation path.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Trigger by compiling (no execution needed) a crafted expression that drives `zend_compile_prop` through delayed/nullsafe property handling with a compile-time constant array base, e.g. `<?['']?->\xff;`. Data flow: fuzzer input -> parser/AST -> `zend_compile_expr`/`zend_compile_var_inner` -> `zend_compile_prop`; constant array allocated in `zend_try_ct_eval_array`; op_array teardown in `fuzzer_do_request` calls `destroy_op_array`, which double-dtors aliased literal zvals and causes heap-use-after-free.
